# algolia_api_key (Resource)

Manages an Algolia API key. The key value is generated by Algolia and is used as the resource ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "algolia_api_key" "search_only" {
  description = "Search-only key for the storefront"
  acl         = ["search", "browse"]
  indexes     = ["products", "products_*"]

  max_hits_per_query          = 100
  max_queries_per_ip_per_hour = 10000
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `acl` (List of String) Permissions (access control list) that determine the type of API requests this key can make, e.g. search, browse, addObject, editSettings.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description to help identify the API key.
- `indexes` (List of String) Index names or patterns this API key can access. Supports leading and trailing wildcards (*).
- `max_hits_per_query` (Number) Maximum number of results this API key can retrieve in one query.
- `max_queries_per_ip_per_hour` (Number) Maximum number of API requests allowed per IP address per hour.
- `query_parameters` (String) Query parameters to add when making API requests with this API key.
- `referers` (List of String) Allowed HTTP referrers for this API key. Supports leading and trailing wildcards (*).
- `validity` (Number) Duration in seconds after which the API key expires. By default, API keys don't expire. Changing this forces a new key.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Number) Timestamp when the key was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
- `id` (String) The generated API key value, used as the resource identifier.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The generated API key value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# API keys are imported by their key value.
terraform import algolia_api_key.search_only "1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef"
```
